html:
"Florence" is the map's label, for 1530 and 1600, for the Medici state of Florence, the Duchy of Florence from 1532 and the Grand Duchy of Tuscany from 1569.

The old republic of Florence, home of the Medici bank and the Renaissance, fell after a long siege in 1529 to 1530 by the army of Emperor Charles V. In 1532 Alessandro de' Medici was made hereditary duke. He was murdered by a cousin in 1537, and the young Cosimo I took power.

Cosimo ruled firmly for nearly forty years. He conquered the Republic of Siena in the 1550s, built the Uffizi as offices for his government, and in 1569 the pope made him Grand Duke of Tuscany. By 1600 Florence was a quiet princely state, a patron of art and science; Galileo would soon serve its court. Its later history is under Tuscany.
